          Manchester City 2-4 PSG Stats: Guardiola's Etihad Return Soured by European Champions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 14, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain blew Manchester City away in the first half, and a second-half fightback proved fruitless as the French side prevailed 4-2 at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday night.
Pep Guardiola took in a UEFA Champions League thriller on his return to the Etihad Stadium as Paris Saint-Germain beat Manchester City 4-2.
Guardiola returned to his former stomping ground for the first time since his departure at the end of last season.

But despite a raucous pre-match atmosphere in City's first home game following the guilty verdict in the Premier League's case against them, Guardiola saw his old team fall 3-0 down inside 32 minutes.
Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Vitinha were on target in an inspired first-half display from PSG, but Erling Haaland‘s double saw City threaten a fightback.

The crossbar spared Matvey Safonov's blushes when he palmed against it in the 12th minute, with Antoine Semenyo blazing over on the rebound, though Marc Guéhi was penalised for a foul on PSG's goalkeeper.
Yet PSG hit the front two minutes later. Fabián Ruiz fed Doué on the counter-attack, and the France winger skipped in from the left before picking out the bottom-left corner with a drilled strike.
PSG were 2-0 up just 99 seconds later, with Doué and Dembélé combining to devastating effect as the latter headed home from point-blank range.
Vitinha tested Gianluigi Donnarumma, who could then do nothing to deny Achraf Hakimi, but the full-back clipped a header against the woodwork.

PSG did go three up in the 32nd minute, however, with Vitinha slamming in first-time from the edge of the box, as City shipped three goals in the first half of a competitive home game for the first time since 2015 vs Liverpool (4-1 loss).

Joskov Gvardiol headed wide and Jérémy Doku shot tamely at Safonov, and Enzo Maresca wasted no time in shuffling his pack at half-time. Matheus Nunes, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye came on, and the latter crossed in for Haaland to head beyond Safonov in the 53rd minute.
Semenyo hit the crossbar, albeit from an offside position, and Ndiaye went close as City urgently pressed for a second, but a Donnarumma blunder dented their hopes.
Donnarumma got a big hand to Maghnes Akliouche‘s shot, yet the former PSG man only managed to spin the ball up and into the net, and he was unable to scramble it clear.
Gvardiol saw an effort cleared off the line and Enzo Fernández rattled the frame of the goal, while Haaland then hit the top of the bar with a towering header.
There was no denying Haaland 57 seconds later, as he coolly swept in from Bouaddi's cutback to reduce the arrears.
Haaland seemed all set to net his hat-trick in the 83rd minute, only to direct an on-the-slide attempt at Safonov.

Former City striker Ferran Torres squandered a golden chance to put the result beyond all doubt when he sent a tame penalty at Donnarumma following Nunes' foul on Nuno Mendes, but the hosts could not make that reprieve count.

PSG put on a clinic in the first half, and even Guardiola, who was so animated he looked as though he wanted to go and join Maresca down on the touchline, must have been slightly in awe of what Luis Enrique's team produced.
It marked the first time City trailed by three goals at half-time in a home game since January 2012, with PSG having hit the target with seven of their 10 first-half shots.
Yet Maresca can at least look at the second-half response with some positivity. He changed the shape, and City dominated.
